name: Moloch
title: Canaanite idol
summary: Moloch (also spelled Molek) was a Canaanite and Ammonite idol who was worshipped through child sacrifice. The worship of Moloch is repeatedly condemned in the Bible as an abominable practice. Several Israelite kings fell into sin by allowing or promoting Moloch worship, especially in the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Prohibition against Moloch Worship in the Mosaic Law
keyEvents.description: God strictly forbids the Israelites from sacrificing their children to Moloch, and the penalty for this is death.

keyEvents.title: Warning against Moloch Worship upon Entering Canaan
keyEvents.description: Moses warns the Israelites not to imitate the abominable customs of the nations in Canaan, including making their children pass through the fire.

keyEvents.title: Solomon's Apostasy and Moloch Worship
keyEvents.description: King Solomon built a high place for Moloch on the mountain east of Jerusalem, influenced by his foreign wives.

keyEvents.title: King Ahaz Sacrifices His Son
keyEvents.description: King Ahaz of Judah made his son pass through the fire according to the abominable customs of the nations whom the Lord had driven out before the Israelites.

keyEvents.title: King Manasseh's Idolatry
keyEvents.description: King Manasseh of Judah made his son pass through the fire and practiced extensive idolatry, which led to God's judgment on Judah.

keyEvents.title: Josiah's Reforms Remove Molech Worship
keyEvents.description: King Josiah destroyed Topheth in the Valley of Hinnom so that no one could any longer make their son or daughter pass through the fire for Molech, as part of his great religious reform.
